title: Quote eligible_leads, not matched_leads — and a count is only valid for the stages it was measured with
summary: Every sizing call returns two counts. `matched_leads` is what the filter selects; `eligible_leads` is Gate 2 — leads still missing at least one REQUESTED stage. On a mature corpus most rows have already been crawled and verified, so 'select 5,000, enrich 200' is the ordinary reading, not an anomaly. eligible_leads is also the number the system itself acts on: the per-job record ceiling, the cost (eligible x stages) and the runtime are all decided by it, so quoting matched_leads quotes a figure nothing will act on. Second half of the trap: eligibility is SCOPED to the stage set, so the same filter yields different counts for different stages — a count carried from one stage set to another is simply wrong. That is why `stages` is required and never defaults on past-runs, count, leads and selections.
references: app/api/v1/dashboard_bulk_lead_sourcing.py — create_bulk_corpus_selection docstring: 'The count returned is Gate 2's, not the filter's'
app/api/v1/dashboard_bulk_lead_sourcing.py — list_bulk_past_runs: stages is REQUIRED rather than defaulted, and why
